taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO, ITIS and Flora of North America accept Sagittaria platyphylla at species rank.
look_here_first: Look at leaf form and the flower stalk together: emergent leaves are usually ovate to linear-ovate rather than arrow-lobed, while submerged leaves can be narrow bladeless-looking phyllodes. On the inflorescence, female flowers are below the male flowers.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — documented from the San Marcos River in a peer-reviewed aquatic-plant survey and Joey's Hays County source video. Travis — City of Austin surveys document delta arrowhead in Barton Creek/Town Lake. Comal — Lindheimer specimens from New Braunfels are preserved at Harvard University Herbaria. Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed county treatment.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Only exact locality/county evidence was counted; statewide or ecoregion range was not converted into counties.

best_field_traits: aquatic perennial with corms and stolons
strong aquatic heterophylly: narrow submerged phyllodes vs broader emergent blades
rough spherical fruiting heads of many beaked achenes
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Submerged leaves may be sessile flattened phyllodes; emergent leaves have long triangular petioles and linear-ovate to ovate blades.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Emergent raceme with several whorls; pistillate flowers occupy lower positions and staminate flowers upper positions.
morphology_keys.fruit: Spherical heads of numerous small beaked achenes.
joey_field_notes: Joey's San Marcos River sequence teaches protogyny/female phase first, the female-below/male-above arrangement, and two leaf forms on the same species.
The heterophylly frame is especially valuable because a submerged plant can look very different from the familiar emergent delta-arrowhead form.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Delta arrowhead commonly has ovate to linear-ovate emergent blades without the deep arrow-shaped basal lobes typical of S. latifolia; submerged S. platyphylla may show narrow phyllodial leaves. Confirm with the whorled inflorescence and fruit characters.
